from math import gcd


def best_average(a: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    pre = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i, x in enumerate(a):
        pre[i + 1] = pre[i] + x

    # Dinkelbach iteration: lam = p / q is always the average of a valid subarray
    p, q = pre[k], k

    while True:
        # Maximize sum over window of (q * a[t] - p) for windows with length >= k.
        # With P[j] = sum_{t<j} (q * a[t] - p) = q * pre[j] - p * j, the window
        # (i, j] has value P[j] - P[i], and we need j - i >= k.
        best_val = None
        best_i = best_j = 0
        min_val = None
        min_idx = 0
        for j in range(k, n + 1):
            i = j - k
            cand = q * pre[i] - p * i
            if min_val is None or cand < min_val:
                min_val = cand
                min_idx = i
            cur = q * pre[j] - p * j - min_val
            if best_val is None or cur > best_val:
                best_val = cur
                best_i, best_j = min_idx, j

        if best_val <= 0:
            break

        s = pre[best_j] - pre[best_i]
        length = best_j - best_i
        p, q = s, length

    g = gcd(p, q)
    return [p // g, q // g]
